How it works

You already have the photos. That is the whole starting point — no reshoot, no scheduling a stager, no waiting on furniture.

  1. 1 Send your listing photos

    Upload the empty-room shots from your photographer or your phone. Straight-on, well-lit photos stage best — we will flag any that will not work before you pay.

  2. 2 Pick a style

    Choose from the four styles below, matched to the home and the buyer pool. Tell us anything to avoid — a seller’s heirloom paint color stays exactly as photographed.

  3. 3 Post within 48 hours

    You get staged images labeled “Virtually Staged,” the original files untouched, and disclosure text ready to paste into your remarks. One revision round is included.

Staging styles

Four looks that cover most Hudson Valley listings. Pick one and it carries straight into your order — every room in the listing is staged in the same style so the photo set feels like one home.

Modern Transitional

Clean lines softened with warm wood and texture. The safe, broad-appeal default — it is the style in the living room demo above.

Scandinavian Calm

Pale woods, white bedding, sage and stone accents. Makes smaller rooms feel bigger and brighter — the bedroom demo above uses it.

Classic Traditional

Rich wood tones, tailored upholstery, symmetry. Built for colonials and older Hudson Valley homes where modern furniture would clash with the trim.

Modern Farmhouse

Shiplap-friendly neutrals, linen, black metal accents, and greenery. The look Dutchess and Ulster buyers ask for by name in new builds and gut renos.

Selected style for your order: Modern Transitional — change it any time before you submit.

MLS compliance, handled

Virtual staging is allowed on the MLS when it is disclosed and honest — and that line is exactly where DIY apps leave you exposed. Every order from us is built to stay on the right side of it.

  • Labeled on the image itself Every staged photo carries a “Virtually Staged” label, so the disclosure survives screenshots, syndication, and social shares.
  • Furniture only — the room never changes Walls, windows, flooring, fixtures, and views stay exactly as photographed. We add furniture and decor, nothing structural.
  • Originals returned with the set Your untouched photos come back in the same folder, so you can post before/after pairs or swap a photo out in seconds.
  • We never hide what is there No covering stains, cracks, or damage, no removing power lines or neighbors, no “fixing” a room’s size. If a photo should not be staged, we tell you.

Disclosure text, ready to paste

Every order includes this line for your public remarks. Copy it now and keep it — it is yours whether you order or not.

Photos in this listing have been virtually staged to help buyers visualize the potential of each room. Furniture and decor shown are digital renderings for illustration only and are not included in the sale. Room dimensions, fixtures, and finishes are shown as they exist.

Questions agents ask

Will buyers feel misled when the home is actually empty?

Not when it is disclosed — and with us it always is, on the image and in your remarks. Buyers understand staged photos the same way they understand a builder’s rendering: a way to see the room’s potential. Agents tell us the bigger risk is the opposite — an empty room that buyers swipe past online and never visit at all.

What photos work best?

Straight-on or corner shots of empty rooms, taken at chest height with the lights on and blinds open. Your listing photographer’s files are perfect. Phone photos work too if they are sharp and level. If a photo will not stage well, we flag it before you pay — you are never charged for a photo we cannot stage.

What if my MLS has stricter rules?

Rules vary by MLS, and a few require the unstaged photo to appear alongside or first in the set. Because we always return your originals and label every staged image, you can meet any of those variations without reordering. Tell us your MLS when you order and we will set the file names and ordering to match its rule.

Why not just use a $16-a-month app myself?

You can — plenty of agents do, and then spend their evening fixing floating sofas, mismatched styles between rooms, and furniture at the wrong scale. We are the done-for-you version: a consistent style across the whole listing, a human check on every image, the disclosure handled, and your time back. At $99–$199 a listing, one extra showing pays for it.
